data.narrative:
Redwood Materials, a Series D climate and energy company founded by J.B. Straubel, commands a stated post-money valuation of $6.0B+ after raising $2.125B to date. Valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private frontier-tech peers in climate and energy (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, QuantumScape, Enovix, and others) alongside 1 public comparable (LNZA).

Two triangulation methods apply to this target. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $6.0B last post-money valuation and applying a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical for Series D advancement, implies a forward valuation of $9.0B. Peer-median analysis, drawing from three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (KoBold at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, Amogy at $700M), produces a median valuation of $1.0B with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity and technology risk variation within the climate tech space.

Triangulating these methods yields a valuation range of $850M (low) to $10.3B (high) with a median of $5.0B. The $6.0B+ stated valuation sits above median, supported by stage-progression logic but substantially above peer-median benchmarks. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peers, commercialization timeline for battery recycling economics, and duration of the Series D round. The wide range ($850M–$10.3B) reflects methodological divergence rather than precision.
